financials_interim.notes: Company (standalone) basis, same period. Marked 'Unaudited *' in the source filing because the current-quarter Company column ALSO includes post-amalgamation results of D P L Premier Gloves Ltd (the amalgamation was into the parent Company itself, not just consolidated at Group level), which is why Company-basis revenue/PBT/PAT show >100% YoY growth -- this is materially inflated by the same one-off inclusion described in the Group-basis notes, not organic standalone growth. Operating_profit derived as gross_profit + other income and gains - distribution costs - administrative expenses (1,784,150+41,645-78,284-922,536=824,975); PBT reconciles exactly: 824,975-144,390+116,063=796,648 (Company has no share-of-associate line, consistent with it being a Group-only equity-accounted investee). No minority interest at Company level (standalone, no consolidation).

Group basis, Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30/06/2026) vs restated-comparable Q1 FY2025/26 (quarter ended 30/06/2025). Operating_profit derived as gross_profit + other income and gains - distribution costs - administrative expenses (5,170,282+152,019-650,362-2,912,572=1,759,367), which ties to Note 7 Industry Segment Results 'Segment results' of Rs.1,759,366'000 (rounding). PBT reconciles: 1,759,366 - finance costs 393,961 + finance income 593,864 - share of loss from equity accounted investee 16,546 = 1,942,723 vs printed PBT 1,942,724 (rounding). All printed quarter-over-quarter % variances in the filing were independently recomputed from the raw current vs prior figures and matched exactly -- no column-swap/dual-rendering artifact was found in this PDF. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: on 1 August 2025 (i.e. AFTER the prior-year comparative quarter but DURING the current quarter), wholly-owned subsidiary D P L Premier Gloves Ltd was amalgamated into Dipped Products PLC (pooling-of-interest, comparatives not restated per Note 5). Note 5 discloses the amalgamation contributed Rs.3,224,111'000 of revenue and Rs.380,123'000 of PBT to the current quarter that has NO equivalent in the prior-year comparative quarter. Stripping this out: ex-amalgamation revenue would be ~Rs.21,800,516'000 vs Rs.22,269,974'000 prior year (-2.1%), and ex-amalgamation PBT would be ~Rs.1,562,601'000 vs Rs.1,516,128'000 prior year (+3.1%) -- i.e. underlying/organic growth is far more modest than the +12.4% revenue / +28.1% PBT headline suggests; roughly 89% of the reported PBT increase (380,123 of 426,596) is mechanically attributable to the one-off inclusion of the amalgamated entity, not organic performance. short_term_borrowings = 'Short-term loans and bank overdrafts' + current portion of 'Interest-bearing loans and borrowings' (excludes lease liabilities). capex = PP&E additions + formers (moulds) purchases + intangible asset acquisitions.

interim_updates.note_text: Dipped Products PLC (Group) reported Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) revenue of Rs.25,024.6mn, up 12.4% YoY from Rs.22,270.0mn, with PBT up 28.1% to Rs.1,942.7mn from Rs.1,516.1mn and PAT (total) up 35.3% to Rs.1,450.9mn from Rs.1,072.5mn. However, this headline growth is substantially a one-off effect: D P L Premier Gloves Ltd was amalgamated into Dipped Products PLC with effect from 1 August 2025 (after the prior-year comparative quarter), and Note 5 discloses this added Rs.3,224.1mn of revenue and Rs.380.1mn of PBT in the current quarter with zero equivalent in the prior-year quarter. Stripping the amalgamation out, underlying revenue actually fell ~2.1% (Rs.21,800.5mn vs Rs.22,270.0mn) and underlying PBT grew only ~3.1% (Rs.1,562.6mn vs Rs.1,516.1mn) -- roughly 89% of the reported PBT increase is mechanical, from the amalgamation, not organic. By segment (Note 6/7): Hand Protection (the core rubber-glove business) revenue grew 21.3% to Rs.17,263.7mn (vs Rs.14,230.5mn) and segment result grew 34.5% to Rs.1,252.8mn (vs Rs.931.8mn) -- but this segment figure ALSO includes the amalgamated entity's Hand Protection output, so even this segment's organic growth is overstated. Plantations segment (tea/rubber estate management, including Kelani Valley Plantations PLC and Talawakelle Tea Estates PLC) revenue fell 3.5% to Rs.7,801.5mn (vs Rs.8,087.6mn) and segment result fell 10.2% to Rs.506.6mn (vs Rs.564.0mn), a genuine underlying weak spot. Below the operating line, finance costs rose 48% to Rs.394.0mn (higher gross borrowings following the amalgamation and continued capex) while finance income more than doubled to Rs.593.9mn (from Rs.284.4mn), and the equity-accounted investee swung to a Rs.16.5mn loss from a Rs.1.6mn profit. Minority interest (NCI, chiefly the listed plantation subsidiaries) grew a modest 12% to Rs.217.5mn, so equity holders captured a disproportionate 40.4% increase in attributable profit to Rs.1,233.4mn. Balance sheet: total assets grew to Rs.90,454.4mn (from Rs.77,651.0mn a year earlier) with total equity at Rs.44,706.6mn; short-term borrowings rose sharply to Rs.12,716.8mn as the Group drew down working-capital and overdraft facilities (partly to fund the amalgamated entity and ongoing capex of Rs.2,522.3mn in the quarter, mostly PP&E for the glove business).
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for DIPD -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. Additionally, note that even the YoY comparison above is distorted by the D P L Premier Gloves amalgamation (see note_text/key_drivers) -- treat the headline YoY % changes with caution as they are not like-for-like organic comparisons.
interim_updates.takeaway: Headline revenue/PBT/PAT growth (+12.4%/+28.1%/+35.3% YoY) is almost entirely a one-off accounting effect of the D P L Premier Gloves amalgamation (effective 1 Aug 2025, so absent from the prior-year comparative) rather than organic improvement -- Note 5 shows the amalgamation alone contributed Rs.380.1mn of the Rs.426.6mn total PBT increase (89%). Stripped of this, underlying revenue was actually down ~2% YoY and underlying PBT up only ~3%, with the genuine soft spot being the Plantations segment (-10.2% segment result) while core Hand Protection growth is itself inflated by the same amalgamation and cannot be cleanly isolated from the disclosed figures.
operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs.25,024.6mn, +12.4% YoY (Rs.22,270.0mn), but ~13% of this (Rs.3,224.1mn) is from the one-off D P L Premier Gloves amalgamation with no prior-year equivalent.
Gross profit Rs.5,170.3mn (+22.0% YoY), gross margin 20.7% vs 19.0% prior year.
Hand Protection segment revenue +21.3% to Rs.17,263.7mn; segment result +34.5% to Rs.1,252.8mn (both figures include the amalgamated entity).
Plantations segment revenue -3.5% to Rs.7,801.5mn; segment result -10.2% to Rs.506.6mn -- the genuine underlying weak spot this quarter.

Finance costs +48% to Rs.394.0mn; finance income +109% to Rs.593.9mn, a large swing below the operating line that itself added ~Rs.510mn net benefit to PBT versus the prior-year quarter's net finance position.

Short-term borrowings jumped to Rs.12,716.8mn (from Rs.9,009.6mn a year earlier) as overdraft/ST loan utilisation rose; capex of Rs.2,522.3mn in the quarter, mostly PP&E additions in the glove business.
key_drivers: D P L Premier Gloves Ltd amalgamation (effective 1 Aug 2025, pooling-of-interest, comparatives not restated per Note 5) mechanically added Rs.3,224.1mn revenue and Rs.380.1mn PBT this quarter with no equivalent in the prior-year comparative -- the single largest driver of headline YoY growth.

Plantations segment (Kelani Valley Plantations PLC, Talawakelle Tea Estates PLC and other Hayleys plantation subsidiaries under DPL Plantations) segment result fell 10.2% YoY to Rs.506.6mn, the only segment showing genuine deterioration.

Finance income more than doubled to Rs.593.9mn (from Rs.284.4mn) while finance costs rose 48% to Rs.394.0mn -- a large net swing below the operating line that also boosted reported PBT growth beyond what operating performance alone would suggest.
